summary: hidden, not from a store, holds deep access
reason: com.sysconfig.service has no icon, did not come from an app store, and holds accessibility, device admin, or a microphone, camera or location grant. This is the shape of stalkerware.
remediation: Remove it, then protect your accounts: change your email and bank passwords from another device, turn on two step sign in, and check your statements. If you believe someone you know installed it, do not remove it yet; keep the phone as it is and get help.
label: Hidden
cardText: No icon, not from a store, and holds deep control of this phone.

summary: accessibility service, not an accessibility app
reason: com.sysconfig.service is an enabled accessibility service and is not an accessibility app. Accessibility services can read everything on screen and type on your behalf.
remediation: Remove it, then protect your accounts: change your email and bank passwords from another device, turn on two step sign in, and check your statements. If you believe someone you know installed it, do not remove it yet; keep the phone as it is and get help.
label: Reads your screen
cardText: Can read everything on your screen and act on your behalf, including in banking apps.

summary: reports to an unrecognized host on a fixed schedule
reason: com.sysconfig.service looked up upd.srv-telemetry.top every 60 s for the whole monitor window. A fixed schedule to a host that is not a recognized service is how monitoring software reports in. It can also be an ordinary app polling its own server.
remediation: If you do not know what com.sysconfig.service is or why it would report on a schedule, uninstall it. If you do, nothing to do.
label: Review
cardText: Reports to upd.srv-telemetry.top every 60 seconds, a host nobody recognises.

summary: starts at boot and ran over 6 h this week
reason: com.sysconfig.service starts itself at boot and ran in the background for more than 6 hours this week, and it is not a music, messaging, navigation or accessibility app.
remediation: Open Settings > Apps > com.sysconfig.service > Battery and check whether the activity makes sense. Uninstall if you do not use it.
label: Review
cardText: Starts at boot and ran over 6 hours this week in the background.

summary: named like a system component, not one
reason: com.sysconfig.service is named like a system component but is not one and did not come from an app store.
remediation: Uninstall com.sysconfig.service from Settings > Apps unless you know exactly what it is.
label: Hidden
cardText: Named like a part of Android but is not one.

summary: installed outside a store, holds a sensitive grant
reason: com.sysconfig.service was installed outside an app store and holds a microphone, camera or location grant.
remediation: If you did not install com.sysconfig.service yourself, uninstall it. If you did, revoke the permissions it does not need.
label: Review
cardText: Installed outside any store and can use your microphone, camera or location.

summary: odd mic, camera or location grant, not from a store
reason: com.sysconfig.service did not come from an app store and holds a microphone, camera or location grant that looks odd for this kind of app.
remediation: Revoke the permission in Settings > Apps > com.sysconfig.service > Permissions, or uninstall it.
label: Review
cardText: Not from a store and holds a microphone, camera or location grant it has no clear use for.
